body:
The Picard tracer predictor in `initialize_implicit_stage_problem!` sweeps the updraft scalars with advection and microphysics only, while the final analytic `u₃` and `ρa` solves evaluate buoyancy and `ᶜmp_tendencyʲs` at its iterate and hold them fixed through the Newton solve. Without entrainment dilution and surface injection, undiluted subcloud air inflates updraft moisture, condensate, and buoyancy in those solves. This PR adds lateral and turbulent entrainment toward the environment value and the first-cell surface mass-flux relaxation to the predictor. In the BOMEX and RICO single-column models (Δt = 120 s), the BOMEX LWP temporal standard deviation drops by 53 % (5.14 to 2.41 g m⁻²; LES: 1.97 g m⁻²), the BOMEX mean LWP bias by 38 %, and the RICO mean LWP bias by 34 %.

The second commit places the updraft microphysics source where it acts. The predictor transports every scalar first; the draft thermodynamics and `ᶜmp_tendencyʲs` are then evaluated at the transported state, and the condensate and precipitation tracers receive `dtγ` times that source. Evaluating the source at the transported state keeps the vapor of each cell consistent with the condensate that arrives with it, so advected condensate is not condensed a second time, and the cached source is the rate that takes the transported condensate to the stage condensate, which the Newton solve keeps frozen. Evaluating the source within the round removes a one-round Picard lag in updraft condensation; with the source evaluated at the swept `(mse, q_tot)` this reduced LWP bias and cloud-base oscillations in DYCOMS RF01/RF02, BOMEX, and RICO, and the transported-state evaluation has so far been checked on a 2 h BOMEX column only.

Also included: the predictor's cell-1 advection factor is zeroed, since `set_velocity_at_surface!` leaves a nonzero covariant `u₃` at the surface over sloped terrain; the surface relaxation rate is a shared helper (`edmfx_sfc_relaxation_rate`) used by the tendency, its Jacobian diagonal, and the predictor; and a unit test checks the predictor against its documented recurrence. Reference counter bumped to 442.
title: Include entrainment and surface injection in the Picard updraft tracer predictor

body:
## Purpose

Make the turbulent flux of cloud liquid and ice consistent with how parcels transport condensate. Down-gradient self-diffusion (#4916) gives a downward liquid flux inside a well-mixed stratocumulus layer, where adiabatic liquid increases with height. Parcels there equilibrate within seconds, so they carry the equilibrium condensate of their conserved variables.

## Content

With the 1M microphysics, prognostic TKE, and the SGS saturation-excess moments, the vertical turbulent flux of each suspended cloud species is the blend

$$
F_{q_\mu} = (1-\lambda_\mu)\,(-\rho K_h \nabla q_\mu) + \lambda_\mu\,(c_{q_t} F_{q_t} + c_{s_l} F_{s_l}), \qquad \lambda_\mu = \frac{\tau_e}{\tau_e + \tau_\mu},
$$

- `F_qt` and `F_sl` are the fluxes of total water and liquid–ice static energy. The energy flux is already built from them: `F_e = F_sl + (h_v + Φ) F_qt`.
- `τ_e = l_mix / (c_d √tke)` is the eddy turnover time, with the master mixing length and no floor (the Damköhler factor of the SGS variance fidelity uses the same rate with the buoyancy-bounded length and a 1 m floor). `τ_μ` is the 1M phase-relaxation time.
- The equilibrium part linearizes the SGS-mean equilibrium condensate that the microphysics relaxes toward:
  - `c_qt = C χ_μ / (1 + C γ)` and `c_sl = −c_qt (∂q_sat/∂T)/c_p`.
  - `C = Φ(λ_eq/σ_S)` is the cloudy fraction of the equilibrium condensate `max(0, λ_eq + S′)` of the 1M node rule, with the multiplier and width of `ᶜsgs_moments`; `χ_μ` is the phase share and `γ = (L/c_p) ∂q_sat/∂T`. With the truncated-Gaussian target, `λ_eq = μ_S` and `C` is the derivative of `E[max(0, S)]`; with a reshaped target (curvature, or the truncated displacement of #4922, whose `λ_eq = −Inf` in clear air gives `C = 0`) the flux follows the microphysics.
  - `1/(1 + Cγ)` is the latent-heat feedback. With an SGS width, `C → 0` makes the equilibrium part vanish in clear air; a width at the `ϵ_numerics` floor (`GridMeanSGS`) switches `C` at saturation, as the microphysics target does.
  - `∂q_sat/∂T` is taken at the cell density, as in the microphysics; at fixed pressure it is larger by `1/(1 − R_v T/L)`, 3–5%.
- The energy flux is unchanged for every `λ`, because parcels conserve `(s_l, q_t)` in transit. A layer well mixed in `(s_l, q_t)` therefore remains a fixed point of diffusion, and with `λ = 1` its condensate flux vanishes as well. Rebuilding the energy flux from the blended species fluxes would reintroduce the `−ρK c_p(Γ_d − Γ_m)` flux that #4916 removed.
- Under `PrognosticEDMFX`, the environment cloud species take the blended flux with the environment state and weight. Draft cloud species keep self-diffusion.
- Other configurations (0M, 2M, 2MP3, no prognostic TKE) are unchanged. The scratch fields of the blend are allocated only with the 1M scheme (`cloud_species_diffusion_temporary_quantities`).
- The implicit Jacobian keeps the unscaled self-diagonal. It bounds the blended diagonal `(1 − λ) + λ C χ γ_μ/(1 + Cγ) ≤ 1` from above, with `γ_μ` the feedback of the species' own latent heat. The autodiff Jacobian, whose precomputed subset has neither `ᶜl_mix` nor `ᶜsgs_moments`, uses self-diffusion.
- The blend flag and its face fluxes are bound once, outside the conditional branches, so the closures over the species capture them unboxed: `vertical_diffusion_boundary_layer_tendency!` allocates 20 KB per call on the unit-test setup (7 KB on main; 42 KB with the bindings inside the branches).

Tests:
- New testset in `vertical_diffusion_tests.jl`:
  - blend-weight limits;
  - `λ = 0` recovers self-diffusion;
  - `λ = 1` in clear air gives no species flux;
  - `λ = 1` in saturated air matches the closed-form coefficients for liquid and ice;
  - `λ = 1/2` is the average of the two limits;
  - the energy and total-water tendencies are independent of `λ`.
  - The synthetic moments set `λ_eq` to the mean saturation excess, as with the truncated-Gaussian target.
- `edmfx_sgs_diffusive_flux_tests.jl`:
  - expected environment cloud-species tendencies are assembled from the blended formula;
  - the `ρq_lcl` Jacobian check is a same-sign upper bound.

Docs: `diffusion.md` and `prophet.md`; NEWS entry.

Review: the sensitivities were checked against finite differences of the fixed point of the relaxation target at fixed enthalpy and total water (agreement to 1e-4 at fixed cell density; 1–5% at fixed pressure, the `1 − R_v T/L` factor above) and against the moist-adiabat fixed point. The latent-heat feedback factor `1/(1 + Cγ)` came out of that review.
title: Blend equilibrium-implied and down-gradient turbulent fluxes of cloud liquid and ice

body:
Where the updraft widens downward (∂a/∂z < 0), sedimentation flux from the environment enters the updraft through the tilted boundary. The tendency is

    a ∂_z(ρwχ) + min(∂a/∂z, 0) (ρ¹w¹χ¹ − ρ⁰w⁰χ⁰) = ∂_z(aρwχ) − ∂a/∂z ρ⁰w⁰χ⁰,

as stated in the docstring and assumed by the Jacobian (update_sgs_advection_jacobian!). The code computed ∂_z(aρwχ) + ∂a/∂z ρ⁰w⁰χ⁰, which removes |∂a/∂z| ρ⁰w⁰χ⁰ from the updraft (and, through the grid-mean residual, adds it to the environment) instead of adding it. The sign slipped in the rewrite of #4721 and has been active since the lateral coefficient defaulted to 1 (#4744) and was hard-coded (#4848).

Bump the reference counter to 444.

body:
## Summary

This PR updates the idealized `RadiationDYCOMS` parameterization ([Stevens2005](https://doi.org/10.1175/MWR2930.1)) in three ways:

1. **Inversion-height detection ($z_i$)**: On a coarse vertical grid, selecting the level with the smallest $|q_t - 8\text{ g/kg}|$ can jump across the inversion to the first dry free-tropospheric cell whenever that cell happens to lie slightly closer to $8\text{ g/kg}$ than the uppermost boundary-layer cell, placing the free-tropospheric cooling term inside the cloud top. The column reduction now selects the highest level with $q_t \ge 8\text{ g/kg}$, falling back to the level closest to $8\text{ g/kg}$ only if the entire column is drier than $8\text{ g/kg}$.
2. **Grid-mean liquid water for optical depth**: Uses the precomputed grid-mean liquid specific humidity `ᶜq_liq` (`p.precomputed.ᶜq_liq`) across all microphysics and turbulence closures when integrating the upward and downward liquid water paths.
3. **Updraft radiative heating (`PrognosticEDMFX`)**: Applies the grid-mean radiative flux convergence divided by updraft density to each prognostic updraft's moist static energy (`Yₜ.c.sgsʲs.:($j).mse`), matching the RRTMGP tendencies.
title: Improve DYCOMS radiation inversion-height detection and heat updraft MSE
